Subject: Vendor onboarding — PO 98765 mismatch & prioritized remit request

Hi Marcus / Redwood procurement team,

We're getting close to our first invoice for project COAST-9 and noticed the PO your intake sent over (PO 98765) lists a Net 45 billing window, while our vendor setup form and AP policy requests Net 30 with an option to enroll in the prioritized-remit lane for 10-day early disbursement. We've attached our payment preferences worksheet to make the mapping clear.

Can we align the PO terms so our AP system can route invoices to the early-remit workflow? If the PO needs to remain Net 45 for contract reasons, can Redwood provide a short memo or payment exception so we can automate routing on our end?

Also: our finance team prefers invoices to reference the project code (COAST-9) in the PDF header — the invoice we received doesn't. That may block auto-ingest.

Attachments: Kepler_Payment_Prefs.xlsx, Kepler_PO_98765.pdf

Thanks,
Ellen Jacobs
Director, Finance Operations
Kepler Analytics

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding — PO 98765 mismatch & prioritized remit request

Ellen — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the payment prefs. I pulled the intake record and you are right: the PO was created with the default billing cadence (Net 45) because the contract template included extended milestone payment language.

Short answers:
- We can update the PO to Net 30 if both legal and the contract owner sign off — that won't take long but needs a quick redline confirmation.
- If you want the prioritized-remit lane (10-day early disbursement), that's something Finance needs to opt Kepler into. @Marissa / @David — can we confirm the enrollment checklist and whether we require a signed AP addendum?

Ellen, can you confirm whether Kepler is able to accept the early-remit settlement terms (there's a small processing fee on your side)? Also confirm the invoice header needs to include COAST-9 exactly as the project code.

I'll hold off on changing the PO until we have internal on the addendum and external confirmation.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Supplier Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi Marcus — thanks for the quick reply.

Kepler can accept an early-disbursement option subject to three items:
1) formal enrollment acknowledgment from Redwood Finance (we need a signed addendum or an enrollment confirmation email),
2) PO shows Net 30 (so our AR rules can map it), and
3) invoices include COAST-9 in the header and PDF metadata.

We can cover your processing fee up to 0.5% for the pilot period if that helps move things along. We can also sign a short one-page AP addendum via DocuSign.

If you confirm the scope (pilot for the first three invoices, prioritized remit up to $75k per invoice), I'll route the DocuSign today.

Best,
Ellen

Marcus / team — looping in Finance ops and payments policy. Quick notes:
- We require the signed addendum for any prioritized remit enrollment. It covers acceptance of settlement fee and updated remittance instructions.
- If Kepler signs the one-page DocuSign we can set their vendor profile flag to "priority_remit" and map Net 30 POs to the early-disbursement workflow automatically.
- For the PO change: Legal needs to confirm the contract amendment. If Legal is not available immediately, Finance can grant a temporary routing override for the first invoice while legal clears the amendment — that's what we usually do for pilots under $100k.

Marcus — I'll prepare the DocuSign addendum draft and share a link. David, please confirm whether we need any additional KYC docs for Kepler before we flip the flag.

Thanks,
